sections.changelog:
Added

  • **Scenario tests (`tests/`).** `tests/run.sh` drives `tests/scenarios.php` against any install with the plugin active — locally or over SSH against the test site. The run builds its own catalogue (terms with a parent/child branch, products with prices, a draft and an excluded record), asserts 49 checks across tokenizing, retrieval, strictness, synonyms, negation, typos, article numbers, category badges, facet counters over a pool, the price filter, pins and redirects, visibility, index synchronisation, the live-search endpoint and index bookkeeping, then removes every fixture and restores the settings — including when a scenario throws. Excluded from the distribution ZIP.

Fixed

  • **Category counts now agree with the results they open.** The dropdown badge and the results-page facets counted on a stricter rule than the result list itself: on top of the strictness floor they demanded the coverage the single best-matching product reached, so a query like "iphone 14 pro" showed 16 next to a category that opened 137, and "a515" summed to 5 badges over a list of 83. The floor is now the one the result list uses; how much of the query a category's best product covers only orders the badges, so the strongest category still leads while the others keep an honest number.
  • **Results-page facets count the pool the page is showing.** They used to re-run the search on their own, which drifted from the list whenever anything shaped it — the results ceiling, the post-type scope, a fuzzy rescue, the multilingual filter. Counting inside the ranked pool makes the number next to a facet exactly what ticking it leaves, and drops one heavy repeat query per results page. A product filed under a child term counts for its parents too, matching how the facet filters.
  • **A glued model code is one concept again, not several.** "a515" indexes as both `a515` and `515`, and each derived term used to seed its own coverage group — so a single typed word demanded, in the badge, coverage that only the whole code could satisfy, while the strictness floor still counted it as one word. Terms are now grouped by the word they came from, exactly as `word_count()` already counted them.
  • **Search-as-you-type no longer prefixes on a bare number.** The dropdown extends the trailing word by prefix, but it anchored on the last term the word split into — for "a515" that was `515`, which pulled unrelated codes ("51549788", "5158") and never reached `a515f`. It now anchors on the word itself, and a digits-only transliteration is no longer used as a prefix unless the shopper is actually typing a number.
  • **Facet counters follow the price filter.** The pool the counters read was taken before the price range narrowed it, so a category kept promising results that a chosen price had already removed, and its cache entry did not distinguish one price range from another. The pool is now taken after the filter. A pool that matched nothing is also no longer mistaken for "no pool given", which used to make the counters fall back to the query and contradict an empty page; and the panel stays on screen while a filter is active, so "Reset" remains reachable instead of disappearing together with the results.
  • **A pinning rule without IDs no longer silences the working one.** `pins_for()` returned on the first line matching the query even when nothing after `=>` parsed as an ID, so the rule below it was never reached — while the Analytics tab's "Pin" button seeds exactly such a line above the existing rules. An unfinished line is now skipped, the way redirects already worked.
  • **An abandoned reindex is picked up in the background.** A rebuild started from the admin screen ran only while the tab was open: nothing was scheduled to continue it, so closing the tab mid-way left the index written but its statistics never rebuilt — which degrades ranking until someone runs a full reindex to the end. A drain is now scheduled as a safety net; it yields while the tab is driving, so a run that finishes in the browser is unaffected.
  • **Live search caches per language.** The dropdown's cache key did not include the current language, while the language filter runs on the results, so on a Polylang / WPML site the second locale could be served the first one's suggestions until the entry expired.
  • **The reindex report counts what the index holds.** It showed how many records the run walked over, including those it then removed as excluded from search, which overstated the index by the number of exclusions.
  • **Bar height and font size state their real range.** The fields accepted values that were silently raised to the minimum on save (15 became 28); the hint now names the range that is actually stored.
